title: Hokitika Gorge Walk: Hokitika Gorge Scenic Reserve, West Coast region
overview: Hokitika Gorge is one of the West Coast’s most scenic natural attractions. There’s turquoise water, lush rainforest and walking options for everyone.
No dogs. Other pets on conservation land rules.

Easy short walk
Cross the swing bridge and continue for 5 min. At the junction, follow the signs to a second viewing platform with scenic river and gorge views.
45 min / 1.2 km (one way)
The upper Hokitika Gorge suspension bridge is 15 min walk from the junction. At 90 m, the bridge is one of the longest in New Zealand.
After crossing the bridge, it's a 30 min walk back to the car park through rainforest, with some ups and downs.
Hokitika Gorge is 30 min by car from Hokitika.
After about 1.5 km, Stafford Street becomes Kaniere Road. Follow Kaniere Road for 4 km and keep right at the junction with Lake Kaniere Road.
Follow Kaniere–Kowhitirangi Road for 18 km. Turn right at the T-junction with Upper Kokatahi Road. Continue over the bridge across the Kokatahi River. The road then bends sharp left and sharp right.
Drive through Kowhitirangi, then turn left onto Johnston Road, right onto Neilson Road and left onto Whitcombe Valley Road. Follow Whitcombe Valley Road for 6 km.
The car park gets very busy during the summer season (November to April).
Bookings are not required for Hokitika Gorge Track.
Food and petrol can be found in Hokitika (30 min by car).
Kea and weka are protected native birds. Do not feed them.
